parsed.explanation: Federal document and entry regime dominates: X-markers barred, sex-at-birth-only processing, reports of passports confiscated/blocking stranding travelers, a consular cable directing refusal where document discrepancy casts doubt on sex, and possible fraud-based lifetime ineligibility. Federal single-sex facility bar reaches government-funded spaces even in this protective state; federal custody applies conversion-therapy-style policies and birth-sex placement; airport screening routinely outs. Interaction: the state's shield, 1993 gender-identity protections, X-markers on licenses, and 'most protective tier' rating operate only inside the state — federal entry, border, and custody decisions override them. Status: documented.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal regime: X-marker passports stopped (Feb 2025), markers only M/F per supporting documents; Supreme Court allowed restrictions Nov 2025; travelers report passports confiscated or blocked, some stranded abroad. Consular cable directs refusal where document discrepancy casts reasonable doubt on sex, with fraud/lifetime-ineligibility consideration.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiration; fraud finding requires four elements, limited waiver exists, never automatic; legal-aid FAQ guides documentation strategy; suit by civil-liberties union pending.
entry_documents.interaction: Federal entry screening applies at all ports including this state; state document openness (X on licenses, no-document DL changes) does not travel to the border.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-like policies for transgender inmates (hair cutting, hormone removal) from 2026; immigration custody reports forced labor, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse against trans men. Dated state case (2012): trans woman held in men's facility, attacked, no history of identity-based placement.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Hate-crime statute covers gender identity; state abolished trans panic defence (2024); state courts functioning; attacker in the 2012 case prosecuted.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any federal detention overrides state placement norms; state protective custody practice documented only in a 2012 resident case.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal EO bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; 21 state/provinces have bans, 4 criminalize use in some circumstances, one 2025 arrest documented (elsewhere). Universal exposure at federal buildings.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state has no mapped ban; 1993 law bars gender-identity discrimination in public accommodations; state facilities remain open by identity.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State protection governs state/private venues; federal funding rule reaches federally funded spaces inside the state, so the outed traveler carries residual exclusion risk.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders hostile to gender-affirming care, Oct 2025 proposed insurance bar for under-18s, DOJ hospital-record subpoenas; national coverage constraints.
care_services.protection: State shield law (2023): gender-affirming care is public policy, providers may bill insurance, insurers barred from excluding trans coverage; shield blocks out-of-state subpoenas, warrants, extradition and custody-removal orders for families travelling for treatment; conversion therapy banned for minors.
care_services.interaction: Shield protects the visiting family inside the state but cannot bind federal agencies acting under federal authority.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy (May 2026) names 'radically pro-transgender' ideology for identification/neutralization; DOJ reward memo frames 'radical gender ideology'; official rhetoric; 66% public support for birth-sex documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State repealed 'does not condone' statutory language (2023); state-level leadership protective; national employment non-discrimination ruling (2020) still on books though administration directed reinterpretation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal framing raises outing and scrutiny probability at airports and federal desks; day-to-day street life in-state runs on state norms.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal EO directs criminal investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; schools funding conditions; federal facility rules reach school-age spaces the family enters.
minors_guardians.protection: State shield expressly covers families travelling for treatment and blocks custody-removal orders from other states; state conversion-therapy ban; state anti-discrimination covers services.
minors_guardians.interaction: Protective shield is state-level; a visiting family remains exposed to federal document, entry and facility rules the state cannot waive.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific violence figures in dossier (deliberately not counted); national hate incidents include bias motivation regularly; one dated (2012) in-custody assault with attacker prosecuted.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime statute adds penalties for gender-identity motivation since 1993; 1993 comprehensive non-discrimination law operative; trans panic defence abolished; functioning courts documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of state violence data is not proof of safety, but documented enforcement machinery exists and records prosecutions.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Enforcement data for state hate-crime/non-discrimination provisions not sourced; shield-law application to specific cross-state orders unresolved; federal measures partially enjoined, so exposure fluctuates with litigation timing.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Independent July 2026 risk assessment places state in its most protective tier; pending ACLU-style suit on passports; running legal-aid FAQ; documented functioning courts.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Federal remedies are contested and slow; state remedies exist but visitor-facing enforcement data is thin.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower exposure than 0.35-A: no trans-specific entry register or blanket exclusion bar; visa refusal on discrepancy requires documented elements and waiver exists. But the document regime's confiscation reports and refusal instruction resemble its routine, unappealable exclusion enough that the gap is real, not a tier apart.

Similar mechanism — secondary screening, discretionary refusal, slow appeals — but this jurisdiction adds operative state protections (1993 non-discrimination, shield, X-markers) that 0.55-B lacks, while adding a harsher federal document layer. Comparable tier, modestly above.

Below 0.75-C: that anchor assumes trained respectful inspection and recognition of congruent markers; here the federal government affirmatively restricts markers, reports confiscation, and instructs refusal on sex-doubt, a documented universal exposure absent there.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is a protective state operating inside a hostile federal government. State law — 1993 non-discrimination, shield law protecting travelling care-seeking families, X-markers, conversion-therapy ban, hate-crime penalties, 'most protective tier' rating — keeps street, service and care exposure low and remedies real. But the traveller passes federal screens the state cannot shield: passport/visa marker restrictions with confiscation reports, a consular cable directing refusal on document discrepancy, government-facility exclusion, and birth-sex custody practice in federal detention. Severity if outed inside the state is moderate (friction, scrutiny, occasional exclusion), but universal federal document exposure plus custody risk holds the score to roughly 0.63: well above criminalisation tiers, materially below the trained-inspection anchors.
